question.problem:
Which of the following is equivalent to the integral ${\int }_{C}F\cdot \text{d}r,$ where $F(x,y)=\sqrt{y}\,i+{e}^{x}\,j$ and $C$ is the curve $\operatorname{ln}⁡y=x-2$ traversed from the point $A(2,1)$ to the point $B(4,{e}^{2})?$

*Hint: Use the parametrization $r(t)=(\operatorname{ln}⁡t+2)\,i+t\,j.$*
question.worked_solution:
We will use the formula

$$
{\int }_{C}F\cdot \text{d}r={\int }_{a}^{b}F(r(t))\cdot {r}^{′}(t)\,\text{d}t.
$$

First, we need to parameterize the curve. This is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}r(t) & =(\operatorname{ln}⁡t+2)\,i+t\,j,\,1\le t\le {e}^{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

Thus, along the curve $C,$ we have

$$
x=\operatorname{ln}⁡t+2,\,y=t.
$$

As a result, 

$$
\begin{aligned}F(r(t)) & =\sqrt{y}\,i+{e}^{x}\,j \\  & =\sqrt{t}\,i+{e}^{\operatorname{ln}⁡t+2}\,j \\  & =\sqrt{t}\,i+t{e}^{2}\,j.\end{aligned}
$$

Computing ${r}^{′}(t),$ we get 

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}^{′}(t) & =\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t}\,i+\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t}\,j \\  & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\operatorname{ln}⁡t+2)i+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(t)j \\  & =\frac{1}{t}\,i+j.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}F(r(t))\cdot {r}^{′}(t) & =(\sqrt{t}\,i+t{e}^{2}\,j)\cdot (\frac{1}{t}\,i+j) \\  & =\sqrt{t}\cdot \frac{1}{t}+t{e}^{2} \\  & =\frac{1}{\sqrt{t}}+{e}^{2}t.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we can write the integral as 

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{C}F\cdot \text{d}r & ={\int }_{1}^{{e}^{2}}F(r(t))\cdot {r}^{′}(t)\,\text{d}t \\  & ={\int }_{1}^{{e}^{2}}(\frac{1}{\sqrt{t}}+{e}^{2}t)\,dt.\end{aligned}
$$
